In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the business cycle in developing countries is not very similar to that of industrial countries, but is also not very dissimilar.
the stylized facts are not very stylized.
the business cycle in the developing countries analyzed is not a simple replica of the business cycle in industrial countries.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

developing countries are characterized by more pronounced fluctuations in real variables than in monetary and fiscal variables, and the business cycle in developing countries is more closely linked to industrial country economic activity than to the behavior of their monetary and fiscal aggregates.

, while developing countries share some business cycle characteristics with industrial countries (e. g., procyclical wages and counter cyclicity in government expenditure), there are also some important differences (e.g., the velocity of money is counter cyclical in developing countries).
, although developing countries share some macroeconomic features with industrial economies, they also display a number of unique characteristics.
The main takeaway from our work is that
there is no single business cycle pattern in developing countries.
there is no single pattern of macroeconomic fluctuations across developing countries, but that some regularities are common across these countries.
the stylized facts of the business cycle for these countries are not very different from those of industrial countries, despite their very different institutional and economic structures.
